influenceLayers.title: TCM Framework
paragraphs:
In Traditional Chinese Medicine, the Spleen (Pi) governs transportation and transformation—the ability to process food, experiences, and emotions into usable energy
and waste. The Kidney (Shen) stores Jing—the deep reserve that metabolizes essence. The emotion of the Spleen is worry—the endless loop of "what if," "should
have," "if only." The emotion of the Kidney is fear—the terror of not being supported, of collapse, of not being held.
When you chronically worry and live in fear, Spleen Qi becomes deficient. The Spleen fails to "lift" the Qi and transform fluids into energy. Instead, fluids congeal into
"dampness." Dampness sinks. It accumulates in the lower belly. This is not fat. This is stagnation. It is the physical manifestation of emotions that never got processed,
weight that was never released.

influenceLayers.title: Jungian Shadow
paragraphs:
You have suppressed the archetype of the Vulnerable One—the part that knows how to be seen, to be felt, to be held. Somewhere early, you learned that being visible
was dangerous. That being soft meant being hurt. That being small meant being safe. Your shadow self—the one who wants to be seen, to be held, to take up space
—has been locked in the basement.
But the body does not forget. The body builds a fortress. The fortress is the belly. The belly is the armor. The weight is not laziness. It is protection. It is the physical
manifestation of the belief that if you take up less space, you will be safer. The belly is not the enemy. The belly is the body's way of saying "I need a buffer. I need a
wall. I need to be protected from the things that hurt me."

Inhale through the nose for 4 seconds.
Exhale through the mouth for 8 seconds.
Whisper: I release what I no longer need to carry. I support my body without punishment.
Choose one action: walk, hydrate, plan protein/fiber, sleep earlier, review meds, or schedule labs.

naturalSupport.title: Supportive Care
naturalSupport.disclaimer: Supportive care is not a cure. Weight Issues (Thighs) may require medical evaluation, diagnosis, and condition-specific treatment.

items.label: Medical review
items.detail: Review A1c/glucose, lipids, blood pressure, thyroid if indicated, sleep apnea, medications, PCOS/menopause/pregnancy context, pain, and mood.

items.label: Food structure
items.detail: Protein, fiber, whole foods, hydration, and regular meals can support appetite and metabolic health.

items.label: Movement
items.detail: Use realistic movement that respects pain, disability, strength, and current capacity.

items.label: Strength training
items.detail: Build muscle and function even though spot fat loss is a lying little sales goblin.

avoid: Do not ignore sudden gain, swelling, shortness of breath, chest pain, rapid unexplained change, or severe fatigue.
Do not use starvation, purging, laxatives, dangerous supplements, or shame as a weight plan.

brutalActions: Check labs and meds.
Pick one sustainable routine.
Stop letting shame manage the project.
Remove one box from the thighs story today.

clinical.mechanism: Weight distribution around the thighs can reflect genetics, sex hormones, age, muscle mass, total body fat, visceral/subcutaneous fat, insulin resistance, medications, sleep, stress, menopause/pregnancy history, activity, pain, disability, and medical conditions. Spot reduction is not how fat loss works, because biology enjoys disappointing marketing departments.
protocol: Track sudden changes, swelling, pain, shortness of breath, diabetes symptoms, thyroid symptoms, medications, sleep apnea, PCOS/menopause/pregnancy context, eating disorder symptoms, and overall metabolic markers.
Use symptom tracking and medical evaluation when symptoms are severe, persistent, recurrent, progressive, or paired with red flags.
Do not replace diagnosis or prescribed treatment with symbolic interpretation.
citations: Educational reflection only; not a substitute for medical care.

witty.metaphorText: The thighs room is full of boxes: biology, hormones, sleep debt, food patterns, meds, stress, and emotional junk mail.
witty.wittyAdvice: Sort one box at a time. Do not burn the house down.

brutal.realityCheck: You may have a weight issues (thighs) concern. You may also have an accumulation-and-load pattern.

critical_alerts: Sudden rapid weight gain, swelling in legs/abdomen, shortness of breath, or chest pain
Severe fatigue, unexplained weight change, weakness, or thyroid symptoms
Pregnancy possibility, fluid retention, kidney/liver/heart symptoms, or medication-related gain
Excessive thirst, frequent urination, blurry vision, or diabetes symptoms
Eating disorder symptoms: bingeing, purging, restriction, laxative misuse, or severe distress
Severe depression, self-harm thoughts, or body-image crisis
seek_immediate_care_if: Weight gain occurs with shortness of breath, chest pain, severe swelling, fainting, confusion, or feeling medically unsafe
Eating behaviors or body distress involve self-harm, purging, or medical instability
Rapid unexplained gain suggests fluid retention or serious illness
schedule_care_if: Weight is affecting health, mobility, sleep, blood pressure, glucose, lipids, pain, or mood
You need medication review, lab screening, sleep apnea evaluation, hormone review, or obesity treatment options
Weight change is rapid, unexplained, or distressing
medical_safety.self_care_allowed_if: Sustainable food structure, movement, sleep support, stress reduction, and tracking can support weight health without red flags.
medical_safety.do_not_ignore: Weight is complex and not a moral failure. Sudden changes and metabolic symptoms need medical evaluation.
medical_safety.disclaimer: This app is for education and self-reflection only. It does not diagnose, treat, prevent, or cure disease.
